prompt: honest question: is it worth learning to cook properly if i live alone and mostly eat the same five things
text:
Yes, but probably not in the way "cooking properly" suggests. You don't need to learn a wide range of recipes. A few core skills will make your five things better, cheaper, and less boring.

**What's worth learning:**
- **Seasoning and salt.** This is the biggest gap between food that's fine and food that's good.
- **Heat control.** Knowing how to brown things instead of steaming them improves almost everything.
- **Basic knife work.** This mostly makes prep faster and less annoying.
- **Cooking in batches.** This matters a lot when you live alone and eat the same meals.

**What's probably not worth it:**
- Learning dozens of new recipes you'll make once.
- Buying specialty gear or ingredients for dishes you won't repeat.
- Classic technique drills, unless you enjoy them.

**Why it still pays off even with five meals:**
- You can make each of the five noticeably better, so repetition bothers you less.
- You'll spend less on takeout when you're tired of those five.
- Small variations (a new sauce, spice, or side) can make one dish feel like several.

If cooking feels like a chore, skip the "proper" project and improve your five meals one at a time. If you find it fun, learning more will be a hobby, and that's a fine reason too.

What are your five things? I can suggest which skills would help most.
